md_description: Workflow for protein crystallography crystallization trials using defined buffer solutions to maintain protein stability and solubility. The pipeline covers protein-buffer trial preparation, crystallization observation capture, and computational assessment of crystal quality to support optimization of crystallization conditions for structural analysis.

protein_sample.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the purified protein starting material, not any trial preparation, incubation, imaging, or analysis settings. Because the DAG already contains a dedicated buffer_solution entity and downstream process nodes for mixing and crystallization, I avoided any fields about buffer composition, pH, crystallization conditions, or outputs. I also avoided repeating generic sample identifiers unless they are essential root-level identity fields; the focus here is on what the protein sample is and where it came from, sufficient to distinguish and reuse the material in crystallography trials.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the purified protein material used as the starting object for crystallization trials; use a stable lab sample ID format such as PS-001 or SAMPLE_2026_0001. Recorded at sample registration before any mixing with buffer solutions.
Common or project-specific name of the protein sample, for example the target protein name or construct name. Recorded at the time the purified material is entered into the crystallization workflow.

Reference accession or construct identifier for the protein material, such as UniProt accession, gene construct ID, or plasmid/clone identifier. Recorded once for the starting sample to support traceability and reuse.

Biological source organism from which the protein was expressed or originally derived, for example Homo sapiens, Escherichia coli, or a specific strain designation. Recorded as an intrinsic origin attribute of the purified sample.

Purification status of the protein material at the time it enters crystallization trials, such as purified, affinity_purified, size_exclusion_purified, or polished. This describes the sample identity and preparation state, not the crystallization trial itself.

Measured concentration of the purified protein sample at the point it is aliquoted for crystallization setup, reported in mg/mL. Typical crystallization working ranges are about 1 to 100 mg/mL depending on protein and assay design.

Buffer system in which the purified protein is stored or formulated before crystallization setup, for example Tris, HEPES, phosphate, or acetate. Record the formulation associated with the protein sample only; do not include trial buffer composition here.

Temperature in degrees Celsius at which the purified protein sample is stored before use in crystallization trials, for example 4, -20, or -80. Record at sample storage or retrieval time as part of the material's handling history.

Storage condition category for the purified protein sample before crystallization, indicating how the sample is preserved prior to use. Examples include refrigerated, frozen, or liquid_nitrogen_stored.

buffer_solution.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic attributes of the prepared buffer formulation itself: its composition, pH, batch identity, and procurement provenance. I excluded crystallization setup parameters, incubation conditions, imaging details, and any downstream crystal outcomes because those belong to Process, Capture, Signal, or Derivative nodes. I also avoided duplicating protein_sample identifiers or any trial-mixture fields. The fields are chosen to let users distinguish buffer lots and reproduce the exact buffer formulation used in protein crystallography trials.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared buffer solution used in crystallization trials; use a stable lab ID format such as BUF-001 or BUFFER_2026_0001. Record at buffer preparation or inventory registration.

Common name or formulation label for the buffer solution, for example HEPES buffer, Tris-HCl buffer, or sodium acetate buffer. Recorded as the identity of the solution before it is used in crystallization setup.

Text description of the buffer composition, including solutes and their nominal concentrations, for example 0.1 M HEPES, 0.2 M sodium chloride, 20% PEG 3350. Record the formulation as prepared, not as added during a specific trial.

Measured pH of the prepared buffer solution at the time of preparation or QC, typically reported at room temperature or the specified measurement temperature. Typical crystallization buffer pH values are about 3 to 10.
Manufacturer or in-house batch number for the specific buffer preparation, used to trace lot-to-lot variation. Record exactly as printed on the label or preparation record, for example B2026-014.

Name of the supplier or internal source that provided the buffer components or prepared buffer solution, for example Sigma-Aldrich, Thermo Fisher, or in-house preparation. Recorded at inventory or receipt time.

Supplier catalog number or product code associated with the buffer formulation or major buffer component, for example H8284 or 12345-67-8. Record the code used to order or identify the exact buffer product.
Date on which the buffer solution was prepared or received into inventory, recorded as a calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD). Useful for tracing freshness and batch history.

Temperature in degrees Celsius at which the prepared buffer solution is stored before use in crystallization trials, for example 4, 20, or -20 depending on formulation stability. Recorded at storage registration time.
Sterility or filtration status of the buffer solution at the time it is made available for crystallization use. Indicates whether the solution was sterilized or filtered for experimental handling.

set_crystallization_trial.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the protocol and operational details of combining the protein sample with the buffer solution to create the trial mixture. I did not repeat protein_sample or buffer_solution identity/provenance fields because those belong to upstream Entity nodes, and I did not add incubation, imaging, raw image, or analysis outputs because those are downstream nodes. I also included the operating agent properties required for process nodes: the software/hardware rule does not apply here, so no instrument/software metadata were added. The fields focus on enough preparation detail to reproduce the crystallization drop setup without describing the resulting mixture as an Entity.

md_schema.descr: Person or role responsible for assembling the crystallization trial, recorded at the time the drop or trial mixture is prepared. Use a stable identifier or role label such as researcher_01 or primary_operator.
Calendar date when the protein sample and buffer solution were combined to establish the crystallization trial, recorded as YYYY-MM-DD.

Ratio of protein sample to buffer solution used when establishing the crystallization drop, reported as a unitless ratio such as 1:1, 2:1, or 3:2. This is measured during setup, before incubation begins.
Total volume of the crystallization drop or trial mixture assembled at setup, reported in microliters. Typical screening drops are about 0.1 to 10 µL, depending on plate format and protocol.
Volume of protein sample dispensed into the crystallization drop at setup, reported in microliters. Record the measured aliquot used during mixing, typically within the 0.05 to 5 µL range.
Volume of buffer solution dispensed into the crystallization drop at setup, reported in microliters. Record the measured aliquot used during mixing, typically within the 0.05 to 10 µL range.
Drop-formation method used to combine protein and buffer for the trial, describing how the setup was made. Examples include hanging_drop, sitting_drop, microbatch, or vapor_diffusion_screening.
Consumable format used to hold the crystallization trial during setup, for example 96-well plate, 24-well plate, or specialized vapor-diffusion plate. Record the plate type at the time of setup.

Ambient or controlled temperature in degrees Celsius at which the crystallization trial was assembled, recorded during setup if temperature is actively controlled. Typical values are 4, 18, or 20 to 25 depending on protocol.

Indicator of whether any additional additive, ligand, or precipitant was included at the trial setup step beyond the protein sample and buffer solution. Use this only to note the presence of extra components, not their downstream effects.

crystallization_trial_mixture.reasoning: This node is an Entity representing the prepared trial mixture itself, so I included only intrinsic properties of the assembled protein-buffer crystallization setup as a material object ready for incubation. I excluded setup protocol details such as volumes, ratios, operator, and method because those belong to the upstream set_crystallization_trial Process node. I also excluded incubation conditions and any imaging or crystal-quality outputs because those are downstream nodes. The fields capture the identity, composition, and physical state of the mixture so a downstream user can track what was actually incubated.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared protein-buffer crystallization mixture or drop, assigned after setup and before incubation. Use a stable lab format such as MIX-001 or TRIAL_2026_0001.

Description of the components present in the crystallization mixture at the time it enters incubation, including protein sample reference, buffer solution reference, and any added precipitant or additive. Record the assembled composition, not the setup recipe.

Physical geometry of the prepared crystallization drop or trial mixture, for example hanging_drop, sitting_drop, or microbatch_drop. Record the realized setup form after assembly and before incubation.
Total volume of the prepared crystallization mixture at the time it is handed off for incubation, reported in microliters. Typical values are about 0.1 to 10 µL depending on the trial format.
Measured pH of the prepared crystallization mixture, if assessed after combining protein and buffer and before incubation. Typical values are in the approximate range 3 to 10.
Qualitative assessment of whether the prepared mixture appears uniform after setup, used to flag mixing artifacts or phase separation before incubation.
Brief visual description of the prepared trial mixture immediately after setup, for example clear, slightly_opalescent, turbid, or droplets_present. Record at the pre-incubation handoff point.

Boolean flag indicating whether the crystallization trial mixture passed setup QC and was transferred to incubation. Set true only if the assembled mixture is considered ready for the next process step.
Calendar date on which this prepared mixture was placed into incubation for crystal growth, recorded as YYYY-MM-DD. This marks the transition from setup to incubation.

incubate_crystallization_trial.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only incubation protocol parameters and operational conditions that control crystal growth. I excluded the trial mixture identity and composition because those belong to the upstream crystallization_trial_mixture Entity, and I excluded imaging and quality assessment because those are downstream Capture, Signal, and Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating general sample or buffer metadata. The fields specify the incubation environment and timing needed to reproduce the crystal-growth step.

md_schema.descr: Person or role responsible for placing and maintaining the crystallization trial under incubation, recorded at the time incubation begins. Use a stable identifier or role label such as researcher_01 or automation_system.
Date and time when the crystallization trial mixture was first placed under incubation, recorded as a timestamp in local lab time or ISO 8601 format.
Total incubation duration applied to the crystallization trial before imaging or removal, reported in days. Typical crystallization screens may be monitored from less than 1 day to several weeks.

Controlled incubation temperature in degrees Celsius used to promote crystal formation, recorded during the incubation process. Common crystallization temperatures are about 4, 16 to 20, or room temperature.

Relative humidity percentage in the incubation environment, if actively controlled, recorded during the incubation process. Typical controlled ranges are 20 to 100 percent depending on the chamber or plate format.
Incubation environment or chamber type used to hold the trial during crystal growth, for example vapor_diffusion_chamber, temperature_controlled_incubator, or sealed_plate_box.
Qualitative description of light exposure during incubation, recorded if relevant to crystal growth stability. Examples include dark, low_light, or ambient_light.
Interval in hours between routine checks or monitoring events during incubation, recorded as the process schedule rather than the resulting observation data. Typical values range from 1 to 168 hours.
Date and time when incubation ended or the trial was transferred onward for observation, recorded in ISO 8601 format or local lab timestamp.

Boolean indicator that the incubation step was completed as intended without process interruption, contamination, or premature drying. Record at the end of incubation as a simple process-quality flag.

crystal_growth_setup.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the incubated crystallization setup as it exists ready for observation. I excluded incubation protocol parameters because those belong to the upstream incubation process, and I excluded imaging instrument settings, file properties, and analysis outputs because those belong downstream to capture, signal, and derivative nodes. The fields focus on the physical status and location of the setup immediately before imaging, so it can be tracked and reused in the workflow.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the incubated crystallization setup or plate position ready for observation, assigned after incubation and before imaging. Use a stable lab format such as GROWTH-001 or SETUP_2026_A01.

Identifier of the crystallization plate or tray holding the incubated setup, such as a barcode, plate number, or container ID. Record the physical carrier for the drop or wells at the time of observation readiness.
Specific well, drop, or position on the crystallization plate containing the incubated setup, for example A01, B12, or drop_03. Recorded to locate the observation target within the plate.

Qualitative state of the incubated crystallization setup immediately before observation, for example clear, precipitated, microcrystals_present, or phase_separated. Record the visible condition of the setup itself, not the captured image or computed result.
Estimated volume of liquid remaining in the drop or well after incubation, reported in microliters. Typical retained volumes vary by crystallization format and evaporation rate.

Indicator of whether the incubated setup remained physically intact and suitable for observation, for example no leak, no desiccation, or no contamination. This is assessed on the setup just before capture.
Boolean flag indicating that the incubated crystallization setup is ready to be sent to the imaging capture step. Set true when the setup is present, intact, and positioned for observation.

image_crystallization_setup.reasoning: This node is a Capture node, so I included only the measurement session and instrument configuration used to image the crystallization setup. I did not include sample or plate properties from the upstream growth setup entity, and I did not include file format, image dimensions, or quality metrics because those belong to the downstream raw_crystallization_images signal. I also followed the agent rule by describing the imaging hardware manufacturer, model, and serial number here. The resulting fields are limited to how the observation was acquired, which is the semantic territory of capture.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the imaging session used to record the crystallization setup, assigned at the time of capture. Use a stable format such as IMG-SESSION-001 or ACQ_2026_0001.
Date and time when the crystallization setup was recorded by the imaging instrument, recorded in ISO 8601 format or local lab timestamp. This marks the actual capture event.
Person or role responsible for initiating and supervising the imaging session, recorded at capture time. Use a stable identifier or role label such as researcher_01 or automation_system.
Manufacturer of the imaging instrument used to record the crystallization setup, for example Nikon, Leica, Olympus, or similar. Record the hardware vendor at the time of capture.
Model name or number of the imaging instrument used for crystal observation, for example Eclipse Ti2, DM6 B, or MXC-1000. Record the specific instrument configuration at capture time.
Serial number of the imaging instrument used for the capture session, recorded to identify the specific hardware instance. Use the number printed on the device or maintenance record.
Objective magnification used during imaging, reported as an integer or numeric factor such as 4, 10, 20, or 40. Record the setting actually used for observation of the crystallization setup.
Camera exposure time in milliseconds used during the imaging session. Typical values may range from a few milliseconds to several hundred milliseconds depending on illumination and sample brightness.

Illumination mode configured for imaging the crystallization setup, for example brightfield, polarized_light, or oblique_light. Record the active acquisition mode used to visualize crystals or morphology.
Focusing strategy used by the imaging instrument during the capture session, such as manual_focus, auto_focus, or z_stack_focus. Record the method actually used to obtain the observed image.
Temperature in degrees Celsius at the time the image was acquired, if the imaging stage or chamber is temperature controlled. Record the controlled measurement point during capture.

Boolean indicator that the imaging session completed successfully and produced a valid observation of the crystallization setup. Set true when the capture hardware and settings yielded a usable session.

raw_crystallization_images.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only raw data artifact properties: file format, size, dimensions, storage location, and technical quality metrics. I excluded imaging settings and instrument metadata because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded any crystal interpretation or scoring because that belongs downstream to the analysis Process and Derivative nodes. The fields are sufficient for file management, downstream processing, and basic technical QC of the image files themselves.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw crystallization image file or file bundle, assigned when the capture output is stored. Use a stable format such as IMGRAW-001 or FILE_2026_0001.
Original file name of the raw crystallization image as stored by the acquisition or transfer system, for example sample_A01_001.tif. Record the exact filename used in the dataset.
Digital file format of the raw crystallization image, recorded at storage or import time. Typical formats include tif, tiff, png, jpg, or czi.
File size of the raw image in bytes at the time it is stored or imported into the dataset. Typical values vary widely with image resolution and format, from kilobytes to gigabytes.
Width of the raw image in pixels, recorded from the file metadata at ingestion. Typical crystallization images may range from hundreds to several thousand pixels in width.
Height of the raw image in pixels, recorded from the file metadata at ingestion. Typical crystallization images may range from hundreds to several thousand pixels in height.
Bit depth of the raw crystallization image file, such as 8, 12, 14, or 16 bits per pixel. Record the storage representation measured from the file metadata.
Number of imaging channels present in the raw file, recorded from file metadata at ingestion. Use 1 for single-channel brightfield images or higher values for multiplexed capture.
Filesystem or object-store path where the raw crystallization image is stored, for example /data/images/A01.tif or s3://bucket/path/file.tif. Record the persistent location used for retrieval.

Technical quality status of the raw image file based on file integrity and capture usability, such as valid, corrupted, incomplete, or unreadable. This reflects signal-level QC rather than scientific interpretation.

analyze_crystal_quality.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the computational analysis parameters and software agent properties used to transform raw images into an assessment. I excluded raw image file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the computed scores, labels, or summaries because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. Following the agent rule, I included software name, version, and repository fields here. The fields capture enough information to reproduce the analysis pipeline and understand how crystal quality was evaluated.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the crystal quality analysis run, assigned when the software begins processing a set of crystallization images. Use a stable format such as ANA-001 or ANALYSIS_2026_0001.
Date and time when the image analysis process was executed, recorded in ISO 8601 format or local lab timestamp.
Person or role responsible for launching or supervising the crystal quality analysis, recorded at process time. Use a stable identifier or role label such as researcher_01 or automation_system.

Name of the software package used to assess crystal presence, size, and morphology from captured images, for example CrystFEL, ImageJ pipeline, or a custom model. Record the processing software used for this process step.
Version of the image analysis software used for this analysis run, recorded exactly as installed or deployed, such as 1.2.3 or v2.0-beta.

Repository, package source, or code location for the analysis software, for example a GitHub URL, internal Git repository path, or package registry reference. Record where the exact analysis implementation can be obtained.

Named algorithm or model family used to estimate crystal presence, size, and morphology from the images, for example thresholding, classical segmentation, or a convolutional neural network. Record the principal computational approach used in the process.
Image channel or modality used as input for the analysis, for example brightfield, polarized_light, or fluorescence. Record the channel actually analyzed from the raw crystallization images.

Free-text or structured description of key analysis settings used during the run, such as segmentation thresholds, model confidence cutoff, or size filters. Record the parameters that materially affect output reproducibility.
Boolean indicator that the analysis process completed successfully and produced output from the captured images. Set true only when processing finished without software or file errors.

crystallization_assessment.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed-result fields that summarize the analysis output across buffer conditions. I excluded raw image properties and capture settings because those belong to upstream Signal and Capture nodes, and I excluded software implementation details because those belong to the upstream analysis Process node. The fields describe the derived assessment content, its scoring dimensions, and summary quality indicators needed for downstream comparison and optimization of crystallization conditions.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed crystallization assessment result, assigned when analysis outputs are compiled. Use a stable format such as ASMT-001 or RESULT_2026_0001.
Date and time when the crystallization assessment was generated, recorded in ISO 8601 format or local lab timestamp.

Reference to the buffer condition or buffer solution identifier associated with this assessment, used to compare outcomes across crystallization trials. Use the upstream buffer or condition ID rather than repeating full composition here.

Computed score indicating whether crystals are present in the analyzed condition, typically normalized on a 0 to 1 or 0 to 100 scale depending on the analysis pipeline. Record the numeric output produced by the assessment algorithm.

Computed score or summary metric for crystal size in the assessed condition, reported in the scale used by the analysis workflow. This is derived from the analyzed images and reflects relative or absolute size depending on the algorithm.

Computed score for crystal morphology quality, such as shape regularity, edge definition, or habit consistency, produced by the assessment algorithm. Record the numeric output used for downstream comparison.

Derived ranking or ordinal class summarizing the overall crystallization outcome for a buffer condition, used for condition optimization. Typical values might indicate poor, moderate, good, or top condition depending on the scoring scheme.

Computed priority label indicating how strongly this condition should be pursued in follow-up crystallization optimization, based on the assessment output. Use the categorization defined by the analysis or review workflow.
Numeric confidence or reliability score associated with the computed assessment, reflecting the stability of the output given the analyzed images. Record the value output by the assessment pipeline.
Concise textual summary of the computed crystallization outcome for the condition, including notable crystal presence, size, and morphology observations as reported by the downstream result object.
